title: Tanzanian Vegetable Samosa
community: Urban Tanzania — the vegetarian street samosa
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Sambusa ya Mboga — crispy triangular pastries filled with spiced potato, peas, onion, and coriander, deep-fried golden. The vegetarian street samosa — as beloved as the meat version, and completely satisfying on its own.
longDesc: Vegetable samosa is the option for the growing number of urban Tanzanians who prefer vegetarian street food, and for the population that eats no meat at certain times. The spiced potato and pea filling is as satisfying as the beef version.
ingredients: 4 medium potatoes — boiled and diced small
steps: Make filling: heat oil. Cook onion, garlic, ginger, chilli until golden.
Add diced potato and peas. Toss to coat. Cook 5 minutes. Add coriander. Cool completely.
Fill and seal as per TZA176 instructions.
Fry at 175°C for 4 minutes until deep golden.
chefTips: Dice potatoes small — they must fit in the samosa without bulging.
Filling must be cool and dry before using.
cookingScience: See TZA176 for samosa cooking science.
sustainabilityTips: Plant-based filling — lowest environmental impact street food.
culturalNote: Vegetable samosa fills the same role as meat samosa in Tanzania's street food economy — fast, affordable, portable — while serving the growing demand for plant-based options from Tanzania's diverse population.
